instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Not About Who Lost
cards.instruction: Keep the conversation focused on rules, effort, or next steps instead of the result that embarrasses you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I handed in our quiz sheet when that team did. Let's review our preparation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They'd finished. We'd only answered two questions. We came last.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, an early submission. We should concentrate on the hand-in procedure.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. Here's a blank practice sheet. I'll say when it's finished; you hand it in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Give me a confident nod when it's ready. That's the signal I'll be watching.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I stopped at the barrier with that man in the bright vest. Let's talk about pacing for the next race.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He's a marshal. You followed him off the course and finished last.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right, course inspection. Next time I'll follow someone setting a proper pace.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Follow me. I'll be running the whole distance.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Run straight past the man in the vest. I'll match you step for step.

cards.title: Let Them Think They Won
cards.instruction: Protect someone’s confidence by hiding how much you softened the challenge, changed the terms, or withheld an advantage.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A clean win. Keep the board as it is; you should be proud.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You took your queen off when I put away a spare pawn. Why?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Standard opening. Your rook still had to find its way to my king.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Let's play again with your queen on. I want to know I can beat your whole side.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Same winning method, more pieces to get past. Show me that rook again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You won, Mum. Put the ribbon on your cake.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You pulled yours out when the baker withdrew hers. Hers was raw; yours wasn't.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, professional standards. There were seven other cakes for you to beat.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then share the prize money with me. I don't want a present disguised as a win.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put it toward your next entry. You don't owe me half a win just because my cake stayed in the kitchen.

cards.title: Admit What You Wanted
cards.instruction: Maneuver them into revealing which outcome they truly wanted before you explain your own stake.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I put my hand up with yours. Before the result comes in, who did you want to win?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We volunteered to count votes. That wasn't a vote for either candidate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Counting preferences. Let's start with yours.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Maya. Weren't you the one who nominated Ruth?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I was. Now tell me what you liked about Maya before you start apologizing for choosing her.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've snapped my folder shut like you. Decision made. Which job were you hoping I'd take?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My folder's empty. Both your unsigned contracts are still in yours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Signatures come after decisions. Local or abroad: what did you want?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Local. I don't want to move, but I didn't want that to choose for you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I chose abroad. Keep telling me why you want to stay; I haven't signed anything.

cards.title: Investment in the Next Round
cards.instruction: Describe defeat, penalty, or a bad bargain as a deliberate investment in a larger future win.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The entry fee wasn't wasted. We're buying a better chance at next year's dog show.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You put a blue ribbon on our dog because the judge did. She was marking a winner; you got us disqualified.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, testing how the judging works before we compete seriously.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They run free training sessions. We could learn the routine without entering.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Book us in. I'll watch the winners, and next year we won't spend the entry fee discovering where a ribbon goes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I bought six trays when that stallholder bought six. This will pay off next market day.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She runs a soup stall. We've bought six trays of tomatoes for our book stall.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Precisely, learning the food market before expanding. What will she give us for them?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Half what we paid. And she offered us the empty pitch beside her next Saturday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take it. The loss bought us a place beside the only person here who knows how to sell a tomato.

cards.title: I Know How to Win This
cards.instruction: Perform mastery of the rules, odds, and consequences while improvising every decision.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You moved your marker to ten, so I've moved mine there. Strong opening.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I just scored ten points. We haven't started your turn.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. Checking the scoring range before I commit to a move.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Put it back at zero. You only move it after you score.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Zero, then. No point exposing my scoring strategy before my turn.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've folded my ticket into quarters like you. Much better odds that way.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm folding the numbered stubs for the drum. Your ticket stays with you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Precisely. A compact record of my entry. Which number are you putting in?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The same number as yours. Keep yours flat so we can match them if you win.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then flatten mine before the draw. I intend to be ready when you call my number.
